simple.meaning: שַׁיִט (shayiṭ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “an oar ; a scourge (figuratively).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 28:15. The surrounding contexts include covenant.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁיִט (H7885) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שַׁיִט (shayiṭ) / H7885 is traced through Isaiah 28:15, Isaiah 33:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H7885. shayit שַׁ֫יִט noun [masculine] rowing (as whipping, lashing the water); — only ׳אֳנִישֿׁ Isa 33:21 rowing vessel ; — 28:15 Kt see שׁוֺט . above [ שׁוּט ] verb denominative row ; — Participle plural שָׁטִים rowers Ezek 27:8 ; 27:26 (of Tyre as ship).

occurrences.englishText: “Because you have said, ‘We have made a covenant with death, and we are in agreement with Sheol. * Sheol is the place of the dead. When the overflowing scourge passes through, it won’t come to us; for we have made lies our refuge, and we have hidden ourselves under falsehood.’ ”
